# Pirate radio: a cicada broadcasts in FM on 433 MHz

**Admin > Radio pirate**: the cicada broadcasts sound in **narrow band FM (NFM)** on 433 MHz, with the CC1101 radio
of the badge. You listen to it with a **Portapack** (HackRF), an **SDR** (RTL-SDR + SDR#, GQRX, SDR++...) or
**another cicada** ("Écouter la radio pirate", listen to the pirate radio). Three sources: a melody generated by the
badge ("Au clair de la lune", public domain, no SD card needed), a **1 kHz tone** (for the measures) or a **WAV file**
of the SD card (`MUSIQUE` folder).

*Version française : [radio_pirate.md](../fr/radio_pirate.md).*

> **Legal note.** The 433.05 - 434.79 MHz band is an ISM / SRD band (short range devices): in France and in Europe,
> transmitting there is free under conditions (effective radiated power ≤ 10 mW, duty cycle limited depending on the
> use). It is **not** a broadcasting band: keep the Radio pirate for **short tests**, at **low power** (-10 dBm by
> default), in the room, without disturbing the other users of the band (remote controls, sensors...). This is why
> it is only available **from the admin mode**, and the transmission stops by itself after **10 minutes**.

## How it works

The CC1101 cannot do analog FM: it does digital modulation (2-FSK, GFSK, OOK...). The trick:

1. The CC1101 is in **2-FSK, asynchronous serial mode** (`PKTCTRL0 = 0x32`): it sends *f0 + deviation* when its GDO0
   pin is high, *f0 - deviation* when it is low, and it reads GDO0 **8 times per bit** of its programmed data rate
   (datasheet, "asynchronous serial operation"). The data rate is set to the maximum of 2-FSK, **500 kBaud**: GDO0 is
   therefore sampled at **4 MHz**.
2. The RP2040 drives GDO0 with a fast **PWM** of ~**122 kHz** (125 MHz / 1024, 10 bits) whose **duty cycle follows
   the samples of the sound**: 50 % = silence, 0 % and 100 % = the peaks. A DMA channel, paced by a DMA timer at the
   sample rate, copies the samples into the register of the PWM, exactly as for the speaker (`audio.c`, output
   `AUDIO_OUT_RADIO`): no computation by the processor during the transmission.
3. An NFM receiver has a narrow channel filter (~12.5 kHz): it does not see the switching at 122 kHz but its
   **average**, *f0 + deviation × (2 × duty cycle - 1)*: the instantaneous frequency follows the sound, that is
   **FM**. (The frequency synthesizer of the CC1101 also smooths the jumps a little.)
4. The products of the PWM fall at ±122 kHz from the carrier (and their multiples), at about -30 dBc: outside the
   listening channel, and inside the 433 MHz band for the channels offered.

The network of the cicadas is paused during the transmission (`net_pause()`), the radio is borrowed from
`radio_tools.c` (`radio_tools_claim()` / `radio_tools_release()`) then given back to the network, which configures
it again (GFSK profile, sync word, reception). The transmission stops at the end of the track, with the left or right
wing, when the page is left, and after 10 minutes in any case.

## The settings

Flanks: previous / next row; wings: previous / next value; on the last row, right wing: transmit (or choose the
file), left wing: back. Long press on the left wing: quit.

| Setting | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Source | Mélodie (melody), Tonalité 1 kHz (1 kHz tone), Fichier SD (SD file) | Mélodie |
| Fréquence (frequency) | 433.300 / 433.650 / **433.920** / 434.200 / 434.500 MHz | 433.920 MHz |
| Puissance (power) | -20, **-10**, 0, +5, +10 dBm | -10 dBm |
| Excursion (deviation) | 2.5 kHz, **5 kHz** (peak, sound at full scale) | 5 kHz |
| Haut-parleur (speaker) | oui / non (yes / no): the badge plays the sound too | non |

- **Mélodie**: "Au clair de la lune" (~23 s), sine with a small envelope, 16 kHz.
- **Tonalité 1 kHz**: continuous sine at 78 % of the deviation (until stopped or the 10 minutes): for the measures.
- **Fichier SD**: the `.WAV` files of the `MUSIQUE` folder (or of the root), read by the WAV player of the badge (8,
  16, 24 or 32 bits, float, mono or stereo, up to 192 kHz). Recommended: mono 16 kHz, normalized (`audio2wav.py`).
  The sound is sent as is (no pre-emphasis, no filter): a very high-pitched sound widens the spectrum a little.

Radio parameters: asynchronous 2-FSK, data rate 500 kBaud (`MDMCFG4/3` = `0x4E` / `0x3B` at 26 MHz), `DEVIATN`
computed for the measured crystal (`0x15` = 5.16 kHz or `0x05` = 2.58 kHz at 26 MHz), `FREND0 = 0x10` (PATABLE[0]),
PATABLE `0x0E` / `0x34` / `0x60` / `0x84` / `0xC0`, the frequency correction of the radio tuning (`FSCTRL0`, see
Réglages > Réglage radio) is kept.

During the transmission, the page shows **ÉMISSION** (on air) in large, the frequency, the power, the source and the
elapsed time.

## Listening

### With a Portapack (HackRF + Mayhem)

**Audio** application (Receive > Audio): modulation **NFM**, frequency **433.920 MHz** (or the one chosen), filter
**16k** for a 5 kHz deviation (or **11k** for 2.5 kHz), medium LNA/VGA gains, squelch at 0 to begin with.
Come close: at -10 dBm the range is a few metres.

### With an SDR (RTL-SDR, Airspy, HackRF...)

SDR#, GQRX, SDR++: **NFM** demodulation, bandwidth ~12.5 kHz (5 kHz deviation: 16 kHz), centred on the frequency
chosen. On the waterfall, you see the carrier and, on each side, the lines of the PWM at ±122 kHz.

### With a Flipper Zero

The Sub-GHz application of the Flipper does not demodulate audio FM: it only lets you **see the carrier**
(Sub-GHz > **Frequency Analyzer**: the frequency and the RSSI show up when the cicada transmits). "Read RAW" with an
FM preset does not give a usable sound.

### With another cicada: "Écouter la radio pirate"

The second badge is a real receiver for this signal:

1. Its CC1101 is in **asynchronous 2-FSK reception** on the same frequency, with a **wide channel of 406 kHz** (the
   PWM of the transmitter, at 122 kHz, goes through it) and the same data rate of 500 kBaud. Its demodulator outputs
   on **GDO2** a 1 when the frequency received is above the centre, a 0 below (`IOCFG2 = 0x0D`): this bit stream
   follows the PWM of the transmitter, its **duty cycle is the sound** (with a slope of about one half).
2. GDO2 is the "B" pin of a PWM slice of the RP2040: in `PWM_DIV_B_HIGH` mode, its counter counts the cycles of the
   clock (125 MHz) **while GDO2 is high**. A DMA channel paced at **16 kHz** copies this counter into a ring: the
   difference between two copies is the time high over 62.5 µs, exact to the cycle, without the processor.
3. The main loop turns it into sound (duty cycle minus its average), plays it on the speaker and measures it every
   second: frequency by counting the zero crossings, purity of 1 kHz with the Goertzel algorithm, level (amplitude
   in % of the half range of the duty cycle), RSSI.
4. **Frequency correction (AFC)**: the crystals of the two badges differ (up to ±20 ppm each, i.e. ±17 kHz).
   The average duty cycle must be 50 %: otherwise the receiver shifts its frequency in steps of ~400 Hz (every
   250 ms, in steps of 2 kHz when the signal is saturated), only when a carrier is received (RSSI ≥ -92 dBm). If it
   reaches ±32 kHz without finding it, it tries the reverse polarity of the demodulator.

Screen: frequency, signal (dBm and gauge), frequency correction, tone detected (only when it is a real tone:
purity ≥ 50 % and level ≥ 5 %), level and average duty cycle, state of the squelch. Flanks: previous / next channel;
right wing: squelch ("Silencieux") on / off; left wing: back.

On the USB serial port, one line per second (example values):

```
pirate: rx tone 1000 Hz, level 38 %, purity 1 kHz 97 %, duty 50 %, rssi -62 dBm, afc +1191 Hz
```

## Test with two badges

1. Badge A (receiver): open "Écouter la radio pirate", on 433.920 MHz. Plug its USB, open the serial port.
2. Badge B (transmitter, admin mode): Admin > Radio pirate, Source "Tonalité 1 kHz", Puissance **0 dBm** (or +10 dBm
   if the badges are far apart: at -10 dBm one measures ~-97 dBm at 1 m, at the edge of the sensitivity in a 406 kHz
   channel), "> Émettre" (transmit). The two badges 1 m apart.
3. On A, within a few seconds: RSSI clearly above -92 dBm, the correction settles, and the serial port prints
   `rx tone 1000 Hz` (±5 Hz) with a high purity; the speaker whistles at 1 kHz.
4. Then the Mélodie (you recognize it on A), then a WAV of the SD card. Stop: left wing on B; the line `no carrier`
   shows up on A.

## Messages on the serial port

- `pirate: start on 433920000 Hz, deviation 5157 Hz (DEVIATN for 5000 Hz), power -10 dBm (PATABLE 0x34), source ...`
- `pirate: stop (fin du morceau | arrêt manuel | page quittée | sécurité : 10 min max) after N s` (end of the track,
  manual stop, page left, safety: 10 min max)
- `pirate: error, ...`, `pirate: radio busy ...` (OOK receiver active, the talk badge for example: try again
  elsewhere than on this badge).
- Receiver: `pirate: rx start ...`, `pirate: rx tone ...`, `pirate: rx afc at its limit, polarity -1`,
  `pirate: rx stop`.

## Limits

- The "cicada" receiver has a wide channel (406 kHz): it is less sensitive than a real NFM receiver, and more
  sensitive to the other transmitters of the band. The sound received is correct but a little compressed.
- No pre-emphasis nor filtering of the sound when transmitting.
- The real frequency depends on the crystal of the badge (see Réglages > Réglage radio): a few kHz of offset are
  normal, the Portapack tolerates them in NFM 16k.
